original_description: Survey a repository for outstanding work and present it as a single backlog. Use whenever the user types /backlog or asks things like 'what's on the backlog', 'what's left to do', 'what should I work on next', 'list the open EPICs / TODOs / tech debt', or 'what work is outstanding here'. Gathers EPIC docs, ROADMAP items, TODO/FIXME/HACK comments in source, an unreleased CHANGELOG, and open GitHub issues into one list; refreshes a BACKLOG.md; and creates/maintains a docs/TECHNICAL_DEBT.md (seeding it with untracked code TODOs plus an automation-flagged code review on first creation). If a repo has no tracked work at all, propose concrete expansions instead of returning nothing. Make sure to use this skill even when the user doesn't say the word 'backlog' but clearly wants an inventory of what's left to build or fix.

final_description: Use to inventory all unfinished work across a repository and hand back one prioritized list of what's left. Trigger on `/backlog`. Also trigger whenever someone steps back to ask about the state of remaining work rather than acting on a single item: what's left to do or build here, what's outstanding before this is "done", what to work on or pick up next, what to resume after time away from a project, or any request to gather scattered signals — open issues, roadmap, EPICs, TODO/FIXME/HACK comments, unreleased changelog — into one place to prioritize. Use it to start or refresh a BACKLOG.md, or to begin a tech-debt doc by pulling TODO comments out of the source. This is a whole-repo survey of remaining work; don't use it to fix, explain, review, or add one specific item. Fire on this intent even when the word "backlog" never appears.

history.description: Use when the user wants a consolidated inventory of unfinished work across a whole repository, or help deciding what to do next. Triggers on `/backlog` and on any request to enumerate, round up, or prioritize outstanding work — e.g. "what's left to do/build", "what should I work on next", "what's outstanding before this is done", "what should I pick up coming back to this project", "round up the issues / roadmap / TODOs / FIXMEs into one list", or "start a tech-debt doc from the code TODOs". The intent is a survey of everything remaining (EPICs, roadmap items, TODO/FIXME/HACK comments, unreleased changelog entries, open GitHub issues), not fixing one item. Also covers creating or refreshing a BACKLOG.md or technical-debt doc. Trigger whenever the user clearly wants this overview even if they never say "backlog".
